packageRules.description: Group all non-major updates together and auto-merge. bumpVersions is what stops an auto-merged update releasing over the top of the previous one: a merge to main publishes immediately, and the publish overwrites whatever is already at that coordinate. Note this project uses `val VERSION`, not `var`, and plain semver with no prerelease suffix.

Keep gradle-wrapper on its own branch. Updating it makes Renovate run ./gradlew in its container, which fails on this build because it needs JDK 17 and 25 through foojay. While the wrapper shared a branch with everything else, that one failure errored the entire non-major batch, and the last successful grouped PR on the sibling repo was nine months before anyone noticed.

Anything that RUNS the build gets its own branch and a human. Anything the build merely compiles against can batch and auto-merge. Every stuck batch on these repos has been the same shape: a build-system component bundled with libraries, where one incompatible member blocks all the rest. gradle-wrapper did it by erroring inside Renovate's container, which killed the grouped batch on KamiCommon for nine months. com.gradleup.shadow 9.6.1 then did it by needing a newer Gradle than the wrapper provides, failing with AdhocComponentWithVariants.addVariantsFromConfiguration on BOTH repos at once. The first instance was fixed specifically rather than as a class, so the second arrived unguarded. Measured locally: Gradle 9.7.1 with shadow 9.6.1 builds clean, so the wrapper is the unblocker. Expect a shadow PR to sit red until the wrapper moves. That is the signal, not a fault, and it no longer holds a dozen unrelated library updates hostage. Matched by matchDepNames, NOT matchPackageNames: for a Gradle plugin, Renovate's packageName is the marker artifact com.gradleup.shadow:com.gradleup.shadow.gradle.plugin, while depName is the plugin id the dashboard shows. The first version of this rule used matchPackageNames with the plugin id and silently matched nothing, so shadow stayed in the auto-merge batch. Every rule that did work here matches a library coordinate, where depName and packageName are the same string.

NEVER update the per-module server API pins. These are not outdated dependencies, they ARE the multi-version architecture: versions/v1_10_R1 must compile against 1.10.2's NMS, v1_8_R1 against 1.8's, and so on. Renovate's first batch collapsed all sixteen org.spigotmc:spigot-server pins onto 1.16.5-R0.1, which would have pointed every module at one Minecraft version. It also rewrote the tacospigot coordinate from 1.8.8-R0.2-REDUCED-KC to 1.8.8-R0.2-REDUCED, dropping a custom suffix because REDUCED sorts above REDUCED-KC. com.sk89q.worldedit:bukkit is pinned at 6.1.9 because worlds6 targets the WorldEdit 6 API on purpose. There is no correct newer version for any of these.

These CAN move, but each one changes something a build check reasons about, so they get their own branch and a human. worldguard-bukkit and fawe are what justify the Java 17 floor on worlds7, since worldguard-bukkit 7.0.9 is entirely class-file major 61. paper-api drives highestPaperDep, which is what makes v_latest a compile check against bleeding-edge Paper and what triggers paperweight re-derivation. Grouped separately rather than merely automerge:false, because a non-automergeable member inside all-minor-patch blocks the entire batch.
